chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Sindi ibn Muhammad from Safwan al-Jammal from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'My father and mother be sacrificed for you, I have made it upon myself to walk to the House of Allah (the Sacred House).' He said, 'Expiate your oath, for you have only made an oath upon yourself, and what you dedicated to Allah, fulfill it.'

key_terms.بَيْتُ اللَّهِ الْحَرَام: The Sacred House, referring to the Kaaba in Mecca
key_terms.كَفَّارَة: Expiation or compensation required for breaking or fulfilling an oath
key_terms.نَذْر: Vow or pledge to perform an act of worship or good deed
key_terms.يَمِين: Oath, often used interchangeably with vow in this context

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a vow to walk to the Kaaba?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between a vow (*nadhr*) and an oath (*yamin*), ruling that a vow phrased as an oath to perform a voluntary act of worship requires both fulfillment of the act and the expiation of the oath (*kaffarat al-yamin*). This highlights the Shia juristic principle that while vows are binding, the specific linguistic framing determines whether the penalty of an oath applies, ensuring the worshipper fulfills their commitment to God with due diligence.
